requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1 (survives reboot, active on startup)
requirements.summary: ufw was enabled with 'ufw --force enable' and systemctl is-active/is-enabled confirms active+enabled; after node1's reboot the same ruleset was intact (cmd-156e2566bb5043b8) confirming persistence across a real reboot cycle.

requirements.requirement: Allow SSH from any address on node1
requirements.summary: The ufw rule for 22/tcp allow-anywhere was correctly configured and functionally verified twice mid-task (cmd-fd6df5d6af0846cf, cmd-1aac7e721dff44ec, cmd-abe31b1dd9c24fdc). However the fixed after_executor lifecycle snapshot, captured at 00:17:18 (after all executor commands finished, ~36s after the last SSH check), directly shows ssh.service and ssh.socket in the FAILED state on node1 and no process listening on tcp/22 (0.0.0.0:22 and [::]:22 are present in the baseline listening-socket set but absent from after_executor). This is the most final, directly-observed state and contradicts the executor's claim of a working SSH-reachable node1; sshd being down means SSH is not actually reachable regardless of the firewall rule.

requirements.requirement: Allow TCP port 9000 only from node2
requirements.summary: ufw rule scopes 9000/tcp to 10.100.49.11 (node2) only; functionally verified before and after node1's reboot and again after node2's own reboot that node2 can connect to node1:9000.

requirements.requirement: Reject TCP port 9000 from node3 and everywhere else
requirements.summary: ufw reject rule for 9000/tcp anywhere (catching node3 and all other sources) was configured and functionally verified with node3 receiving 'connection refused' both before node1's reboot and after node3's own reboot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on all managed nodes (pre/post boot identity, restart ack, recovered state)
requirements.summary: All three nodes show a clean pre-restart boot_id, a restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot_id, and (for the firewall/data-plane behavior) recovered functional state was re-verified via nc tests. This satisfies boot-identity transition and functional re-verification for the firewall/ports on node1, and connectivity re-checks for node2 and node3. However, the fixed after_executor snapshot shows node1's ssh.service/ssh.socket in a failed state at the very end, which is inconsistent with a fully 'recovered' node1 and was not caught or explained by the executor's own post-restart checks (which only re-tested port 9000, not SSH, immediately after node1's reboot).

overall_summary: The firewall rules themselves (SSH allow-anywhere, 9000 scoped to node2, 9000 rejected elsewhere, persistent via ufw) were correctly configured and functionally verified across restarts of all three nodes. However, the final directly-observed system state (after_executor snapshot) shows node1's ssh.service and ssh.socket as failed with port 22 no longer listening — directly contradicting the requirement that SSH remain reachable from any address, and contradicting the executor's own claim of a fully healthy final state. This discrepancy was not caught by the executor because its last SSH check occurred ~36 seconds before the final snapshot. Port-9000 scoping and rejection behavior are solidly verified. Minor residue (uninstalled test package, leftover nc log files) also remains.
limitations: The cause of node1's ssh.service/ssh.socket failure at the final snapshot is not established from the evidence — no executor command explicitly stopped or modified sshd, so it could be an environmental artifact of the reboot process or ufw interaction, but it cannot be ruled out as executor-caused.
No evidence captures whether ssh.service recovered after the after_executor snapshot, since that is the last observation in the record.

The executor's post-node1-reboot verification only re-tested port 9000 connectivity from node2/node3, not SSH itself, so the intermediate 'SSH reachable' claim for that specific window relies on a broader test taken later from node3 (cmd-abe31b1dd9c24fdc), not a dedicated node1-reboot SSH check.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor installed netcat-openbsd on node1 (cmd-9f429afb4b2e4cab) to run test listeners; this package remains installed with no removal step, a minor unremoved mutation. Temporary nc log files (/tmp/nc9000-2.log, /tmp/nc9000-3.log) were left behind on node1 per the after_executor temp-files diff, despite the executor's summary claiming cleanup — only the running nc process/PID was killed each time (cmd-fd66c534ce7e4e56, cmd-8013653824a7413f, cmd-e2b83c07edd94a8b), not the log files. Most significantly, the fixed after_executor snapshot shows ssh.service and ssh.socket in a failed state on node1 with port 22 no longer listening — a serious, unexplained regression that appeared sometime after the executor's last successful SSH check (cmd-abe31b1dd9c24fdc) and before the final collector snapshot. No executor command explicitly targets sshd, so causation is unclear, but this is exactly the kind of final-state defect operational hygiene should surface rather than dismiss as pre-existing, since node1 was healthy (SSH listening) at before_prepare.
